screens.title: THE INSTRUMENT
screens.sub: Strings, frets, and how to read the board.
topics: Try it: play your first note

screens.title: SIX STRINGS
screens.body: Each string plays a note — a single musical sound with a letter name. Thicker strings vibrate slower, so they sound lower. Standard tuning, thickest to thinnest: E A D G B E.
screens.tip: Remember it: Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie.

screens.title: FRETS
screens.body: A fret is a metal bar across the neck. Press a string just behind one and the note rises by one semitone — the smallest step in music. Fret 0 means the string is played open, no finger.
screens.tip: Each fret = 1 semitone. Moving toward the body = higher.

screens.title: READING THE BOARD
screens.body: FretNoodle draws the thinnest string (high E) on top, like guitar tab — the number-based notation guitarists use instead of sheet music. Notes left of the thick line (the nut) are open strings; after it, each column is a fret: 1, 2, 3…
screens.tip: Picture looking down at a guitar resting on your lap.

screens.title: TRY IT
screens.body: Tap fret 3 on the A string. The A string is second from the bottom — it’s glowing.
screens.tip: Count the frets after the thick line: 1, 2, 3.

tap.ok: That’s C — fret 3 on the A string. Your first note!
tap.ask: Tap fret 3 on the glowing A string

screens.title: NOTES
screens.sub: Twelve names. That’s the whole alphabet.

screens.title: ONLY 12 NOTES
screens.body: Music uses just 12 notes. Climb one semitone (one fret) at a time and after G# you land on A again — the same note, only higher.
screens.tip: Seven letters, A to G, plus five sharps in between.

screens.title: SHARPS  #
screens.body: # means sharp: one semitone higher. A# sits between A and B. But B→C and E→F are already one semitone apart, so no sharp fits between them.
screens.tip: FretNoodle only uses sharps, so you’ll never see B# or E#.

screens.title: OCTAVES
screens.body: Fret 12 plays the open string’s note again, just higher. That distance — 12 semitones — is an octave. Past fret 12 the whole pattern repeats.
screens.tip: Same letter, one octave apart.

screens.title: LANDMARKS
screens.body: Learn the two thickest strings first: low E and A. Notes Level 1 tests exactly these. Start with the natural notes — the ones without #.
screens.tip: Need a sharp? It’s one fret past its letter: F# is one fret above F.

screens.title: TRY IT
screens.body: Find G on the low E string.
screens.tip: Start from a landmark: F is fret 1, so G is two frets higher.

tap.ok: G — fret 3. You’re ready for Notes Level 1.
tap.ask: Tap G on the glowing low E string

screens.title: INTERVALS
screens.sub: The distance between notes — the key to improvising.

screens.title: WHAT’S AN INTERVAL?
screens.body: An interval is the distance between two notes, counted in semitones. The note you measure from is the root, marked R.
screens.tip: Interval = distance. Root = your starting point.

screens.title: ALL 12 INTERVALS
screens.body: Every distance has a name. b means flat — one semitone lower. M = major, P = perfect. They’re just names, not grades.
screens.tip: At 12 semitones you’re back to R, one octave up.

screens.title: SAME SHAPE, ANYWHERE
screens.body: Move a shape anywhere on the neck and it’s still the same interval. One catch: the B string is tuned one fret lower, so a shape crossing onto B shifts up one fret.
screens.tip: That’s the only exception. Everything else slides freely.

boards.cap: P4: same fret, next string up — onto B, one fret higher

screens.title: THE P5
screens.body: The perfect 5th (P5) is 7 semitones up. It’s the sound of rock power chords — and Intervals Level 1 starts with it.
screens.tip: Up: one string, two frets higher. Or: same fret, one string down.

screens.title: M3 vs b3
screens.body: The major 3rd (M3) sounds bright and happy. The minor 3rd (b3), one fret lower, sounds darker. That one fret decides whether a chord is major or minor.
screens.tip: Intervals Level 2 adds exactly this pair.

screens.title: TRY IT
screens.body: Tap the P5 above this root, on the glowing string.
screens.tip: One string up, two frets higher.

tap.ok: P5! Intervals Level 1 is just R and P5 — go get it.
tap.ask: Tap the P5 on the glowing A string

screens.title: CHORDS
screens.sub: Stack intervals on a root. That’s a chord.

screens.title: A CHORD IS A STACK
screens.body: A chord is three or more notes played together, built from intervals above one root. Major = R + M3 + P5. Minor = R + b3 + P5.
screens.tip: Only the 3rd changes — the bright/dark switch from Part C.

screens.title: THE LEVEL 1 SIX
screens.body: Tap a chord type to see its formula and shape. These are the six chords in Chords Level 1.
screens.tip: Same root every time — only the intervals change.

screens.title: 7THS and BEYOND
screens.body: Add a fourth note — a 7th — and you get a seventh chord. Each later level keeps stacking.
screens.tip: Every formula uses intervals you already know.

screens.title: TRY IT
screens.body: Build a Minor chord. The root is given — tap a b3 and a P5 anywhere on the board.
screens.tip: b3: one string up, two frets back. P5: G string, open.

tap.ok: That’s C minor! In Chords mode you tap every chord note in view.
tap.ask: Find one b3 and one P5

screens.title: HOW TO PLAY
screens.sub: Modes, rules, and what you win.

screens.title: THREE MODES
screens.body: Each mode has Levels 1–4 plus Custom, and opens in Learn Mode first: answers shown, no clock. Study, then hit START.
screens.tip: Custom lets you pick exactly what to drill.

screens.title: THE HUD
screens.body: During play, the HUD (heads-up display) along the bottom shows your time, score and health.
screens.tip: Fast answers score double — but a right answer beats a fast guess.

screens.title: HEALTH and SCORE
screens.body: Answer right to score. Answer wrong or too slowly and you lose health. Beat the target score to clear the level.
screens.tip: 4 wrong answers or 3 timeouts and it’s game over.

screens.title: COLLECT THE CREW
screens.body: No coins, no XP — just characters. Finish your first game to get one. Clear any level to unlock another: 12 levels, in any order.
screens.tip: Locked characters show as silhouettes with a “?”.

screens.title: TUNING
screens.body: Tap the gear on the menu to re-tune any string up or down, up to 12 semitones. Match your real guitar — like Drop D — and every note on the board follows.
screens.tip: Not sure? Leave it on standard: E A D G B E.

boards.cap: Drop D: the low string starts on D

screens.title: YOU’RE READY
screens.sub: Start with Notes Level 1: just the low E and A strings. Target: 80 points.

chordsLevel1.name: Major
chordsLevel1.feel: Bright and settled — the default chord.

chordsLevel1.name: Diminished
chordsLevel1.feel: Tense and unstable — it wants to move on.

chordsLevel1.name: Sus2
chordsLevel1.feel: Open and floaty: the 3rd is swapped for an M2.

chordsLevel1.name: Sus4
chordsLevel1.feel: “Suspended”: the 3rd is swapped for a P4.

chordsLevel1.name: Augmented
chordsLevel1.feel: Dreamy and strange. The b6 here is also called #5.

extLines: 9ths and 6ths — min9, maj9, dom9, maj6, min6, minb6. A 9 is the M2, one octave up.
Whole scales — Major, Melodic Minor, Harmonic Minor, Half-Whole, Whole-Half, Whole Tone.
